Step 1: Create configmap.yaml
Inside your bda folder, create a file called configmap.yaml.

Paste:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-config
data:
  APP_NAME: "BDA Application"
  PORT: "3000"


This stores two configuration values.
Step 2: Use ConfigMap in server.js
Add these lines:
let appName = process.env.APP_NAME;
let port = process.env.PORT || 3000;

app.get('/config', (req, res) => {
    res.send({
        name: appName,
        port: port
    });
});


Make sure your server listens on:
app.listen(port, '0.0.0.0', () => {
    console.log("Server running");
});


Step 3: Update deployment.yaml
Inside the container section, add envFrom:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: crud-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: crud-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: crud-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: crud2
        image: bda-app:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: my-config


Step 4: Run these commands
kubectl apply -f configmap.yaml


docker build -t bda-app:latest .


kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml


kubectl get pods


Step 5: Test
Open this URL:

http://localhost:30080/config

Expected output:
{
  "name": "BDA Application",
  "port": "3000"
}
